```yaml

## 2b. E2E workflows

### `/Users/gtrrz-victor/wks/cli/bug-investigation/.github/workflows/e2e.yml`

- Concurrency: `group: e2e-tests`, `cancel-in-progress: true` (global, not ref-scoped).

- Job `e2e-tests`: `runs-on: ubuntu-latest`, `timeout-minutes: 40`, `strategy: {fail-fast: false, matrix: {agent: ${{ fromJson(needs.matrix-setup.outputs.agents) }}}}`, permissions `actions: read`, `contents: read`, `copilot-requests: write`.
- Steps: checkout (`persist-credentials: false`) → **mise via `jdx/mise-action@f10502fc09dadecfefb962fff68ce77213930204 # v4` with no `with:` options at all** → `sudo apt-get install -y tmux` → per-agent install `case` → optional roger-roger verify → `go run ./e2e/bootstrap` → `mise run test:e2e --agent <agent>` (roger-roger routed to `mise run test:e2e:roger-roger TestExternalAgent`, which deliberately skips `--rerun-fails`).
- **Go is never set up explicitly here** — it comes from mise (`mise.toml` pins `go = { version = '1.26.6', … }`). Only `ci.yml`'s `test-windows`, `lint.yml`, `release.yml` and `publish-git-remote-entire.yml` use `actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad… # v7.0.0` with `go-version-file: go.mod`.

Model/concurrency pins: `E2E_CODEX_MODEL` = `gpt-5.4-mini`, `E2E_GEMINI_MODEL` = `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`, `E2E_CONCURRENT_TEST_LIMIT` = 6 (gemini) / 1 (droid) / 2 (cursor).
- Artifacts: `actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7`, `if: always()`, `name: e2e-artifacts-${{ matrix.agent }}`, `path: e2e/artifacts/`, `retention-days: 7`.
- Job `e2e-windows: {uses: ./.github/workflows/e2e-windows.yml, secrets: inherit}`.
- Job `notify-slack` runs only on `push` when either failed; classifies RED (`reliable="claude-code opencode gemini-cli roger-roger"` + windows) vs YELLOW via `gh api …/runs/${{ github.run_id }}/jobs`, then posts with `slackapi/slack-github-action@dcb1066f… # v4.0.0`, `webhook: ${{ secrets.E2E_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL }}`, `webhook-type: incoming-webhook`.

### `e2e-windows.yml`
`runs-on: windows-latest`, `timeout-minutes: 45`, `concurrency: {group: e2e-windows-tests, cancel-in-progress: true}`. Chain: `nightly.yml` (cron) → `scripts/create-nightly-tag.sh` → tag push → `release.yml` (`push: tags v*`) → GoReleaser Pro.

```
# Tag format: v<major>.<minor>.<patch+1>-nightly.<YYYYMMDDhhmm>.<short-commit>

**curl|sh script**: yes, it lives in this repo at `/Users/gtrrz-victor/wks/cli/bug-investigation/scripts/install.sh` and is served from `https://entire.io/install.sh` (the hosting/publishing of that URL is *not* in this repo — no workflow uploads it). ```bash
get_latest_nightly_version() {
    local url="https://api.github.com/repos/${GITHUB_REPO}/releases?per_page=20"
    version=$(fetch_github_json "$url" | grep '"tag_name"' | grep 'nightly' | head -n 1 | sed -E …)
```
Default install dir `$HOME/.local/bin`. There is a second, unrelated `./.cursor/install.sh`.

The CLI itself hardcodes the upgrade commands at `/Users/gtrrz-victor/wks/cli/bug-investigation/cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/versioncheck.go:469-471`:
```go
		return "curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash -s -- --channel nightly"
	}
	return "curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash"
```

## 4. Composite actions

**None.** `/Users/gtrrz-victor/wks/cli/bug-investigation/.github/actions/` does not exist, even though `codeql-actions.yml` watches the path `'.github/actions/**'`. All shared logic is duplicated inline across the E2E workflows (the agent-install `case` block appears verbatim in four files: `e2e.yml`, `e2e-isolated.yml`, `e2e-checkpoints-v2.yml`, `e2e-checkpoint-store.yml`) or lives in `mise-tasks/` and `scripts/`.

## 5. Install docs

`/Users/gtrrz-victor/wks/cli/bug-investigation/README.md`, lines 49-71 (Quick Start) and 113-127 ("Release Channels"):

```bash
brew tap entireio/tap
brew trust entireio/tap
brew install --cask entire            # stable
# brew install --cask entire@nightly  # or nightly
```

# curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash -s -- --channel nightly  # or nightly
```

scoop install entire/entire
```
Line 127 states plainly: `- Scoop: currently supports 'stable' only via 'scoop install entire/entire'`. There is no `docs/installation.md` in-repo (the Discord announce template points at the external `https://docs.entire.io/cli/installation`); `docs/` holds architecture notes plus `docs/install-provenance-plan.md`.

## Gaps worth flagging for whatever you're planning

- Adding a new agent to E2E means editing the same `case` block and the same agent list in four workflow files, plus the `reliable=` tier list in `e2e.yml`'s `notify-slack`, plus `e2e-isolated.yml`/`e2e-checkpoints-v2.yml` choice options — there is no composite action or shared list to change in one place.

- `nightly.yml` has no `timeout-minutes` and does no building/testing at all — it will happily tag a broken `main`, since nothing gates the tag on E2E or CI status.</result>

- `TestCheckpointMetadataDeepValidation` — `e2e/tests/checkpoint_metadata_test.go:15` — deep validation of transcript JSONL, content hash, prompt content.
- `TestCleanCurrentHead` — `e2e/tests/clean_test.go:19` — `entire clean` on current HEAD.
- `TestDeletedFilesCommitDeletion` — `e2e/tests/deleted_files_test.go:20` — deletion bundled with a new file in one `git add .` commit doesn't break checkpointing.
- `TestEntireDisable` — `e2e/tests/disable_test.go:19` — after `entire disable`, no checkpoints/trailers.
- `TestDoctorNoIssues` — `e2e/tests/doctor_test.go:19` — `entire doctor --force` reports clean after a checkpointed commit + push.
- `TestExplainCheckpoint` / `TestExplainCheckpointFromClonedRepo` — `e2e/tests/explain_test.go:19,:49` — `entire explain`, incl. on-demand metadata fetch in a fresh clone.
- `TestInteractiveMultiStep` — `e2e/tests/interactive_test.go:13` — tmux TUI session, multi-step prompts.
- `TestMidTurnCommit_DifferentFilesThanPreviousTurn` — `e2e/tests/mid_turn_commit_test.go:28` — mid-turn commit touching different files than the prior turn; tagged "agent-validation" (run for every new agent integration).
- `TestSubagentCommitFlow` — `e2e/tests/subagent_commit_flow_test.go:17` — subagent creates file, user commits; validates trailer + `cli_version`/`strategy`/`sessions` metadata + session agent field.
- `TestMain` — `e2e/tests/main_test.go:18` — harness bootstrap (not a test).

Count: ~54 `TestXxx` functions across 26 files.

## 2. Best-fit smoke test: `TestMultiSessionSequential`

**File:** `/Users/gtrrz-victor/wks/cli/bug-investigation/e2e/tests/multi_session_test.go:43`

Exact match for "sends 2 prompts, creates commits, verifies checkpoints exist". Steps:
1. `testutil.ForEachAgent(t, 3*time.Minute, ...)` — fresh repo per agent, `entire enable` already run by `SetupRepo`.
2. Prompt 1 (`agents.WithPromptTimeout(3m)`): create `docs/red.md`, then `git add` + `git commit` it. Prompt explicitly says no confirmation, no trailers/metadata in the message, no worktrees.
3. Prompt 2: same for `docs/blue.md`.
4. `testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "docs/*.md")`.
5. `testutil.AssertNewCommits(t, s, 2)` — exactly 2 new commits.
6. `testutil.WaitForCheckpoint(t, s, 30*time.Second)` + `AssertCheckpointAdvanced`.
7. `AssertHasCheckpointTrailer(HEAD)` → `cpID1`, `AssertCheckpointExists(cpID1)`; same for `HEAD~1` → `cpID2`.
8. `CheckpointIDs` → each `AssertCheckpointHasSingleSession`, plus `AssertDistinctSessions`.
9. `WaitForNoShadowBranches(10s)`.

**Cheaper/faster alternatives** if you want the truly minimal smoke:
- `TestSingleSessionManualCommit` (`e2e/tests/single_session_test.go:42`) — 1 prompt, 1 manual commit, checkpoint + metadata assertions. Fastest full-loop validation.
- `TestMultiSessionManualCommit` (`multi_session_test.go:15`) — 2 prompts, 1 user commit, 1 checkpoint. Matches "2 prompts" but only one commit/checkpoint.

## 3. Invocation — mise tasks

Tasks are file-based, not in `mise.toml`. `mise.toml` only defines `test`, `test:integration`, `test:ci`, `check`, `build:windows*`.

**`/Users/gtrrz-victor/wks/cli/bug-investigation/mise-tasks/test/e2e/_default`** (= `mise run test:e2e`), a `/bin/sh` script:
```
#USAGE flag "--agent <agent>" ... default="" env="E2E_AGENT"
#USAGE arg "[filter]" help="Test name filter (regex)" default=""
```
- Exports `E2E_AGENT` from `--agent`.
- If `E2E_ENTIRE_BIN` is unset: runs `mise run build`, then sets `E2E_ENTIRE_BIN` to `$PWD/entire.exe` (if present) or `$PWD/entire`.
- Sets `E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR` to `$PWD/e2e/artifacts/<timestamp>` unless already set.
- Runs:
  `gotestsum --format dots --rerun-fails=1 --packages=./e2e/tests --jsonfile $E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR/test-events.json -- -tags=e2e -count=1 -timeout=30m [-run "$filter"]`
- Then `go run ./e2e/cmd/testreport -color -o report.txt ...` and prints `entire-version.txt`.
- Notes in comments: explicit package path (no `...`) because the wildcard panics the Go toolchain on Windows ARM64; `--rerun-fails=1` absorbs agent non-determinism (max 10 failures before reruns are abandoned).

**Build tag:** `-tags=e2e` (every file in `e2e/tests/` starts with `//go:build e2e`). Package under test: `./e2e/tests` only.

**Sibling tasks:**
- `mise-tasks/test/e2e/canary` (`mise run test:e2e:canary`) — deterministic, no API calls. Builds `entire` and `./e2e/vogon`, runs the whole suite with `E2E_AGENT=vogon` (`-timeout=10m`), then runs `E2E_AGENT=roger-roger` with `-run TestExternalAgent`. Preflights that `roger-roger` and `entire-agent-roger-roger` are on PATH. **No `--rerun-fails`** — deliberately, so real regressions aren't masked. Called by `mise run test:ci`.
- `mise-tasks/test/e2e/roger-roger` (`mise run test:e2e:roger-roger`) — `E2E_AGENT=roger-roger`, full suite, no reruns.

**Env vars** (README table at `e2e/README.md`, verified against code):

| Var | Where read | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `E2E_AGENT` | every `e2e/agents/*.go` `init()` | agent self-registers only if unset or equal to its name. Default = all registered agents. |
| `E2E_ENTIRE_BIN` | `e2e/entire/entire.go:16` (`BinPath()`) | path to `entire` binary; **`log.Fatal` if unset** |
| `E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR` | `e2e/tests/main_test.go:19` | artifact output dir |
| `E2E_CHECKPOINT_STORE` | `main_test.go:52` | maps to `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINTS_PRIMARY`; defaults to `git-branch` (pin is required — the harness's assertions assume v1 branch while first-run enable now defaults to `git-refs`) |
| `E2E_KEEP_REPOS` | `testutil/repo.go:48,774`, `artifacts.go:87` | preserve temp repos + symlink into artifact dir |
| `E2E_CONCURRENT_TEST_LIMIT` | `agents/agent.go:78` | overrides every `RegisterGate` default |
| `E2E_TIMEOUT` | **only `agents/opencode.go:98`** | per-prompt timeout for OpenCode only; default `2m`. The README documents it generically, but no other agent reads it. |
| `E2E_CODEX_MODEL` | `agents/codex.go:226` | Codex model override (CI: `gpt-5.4-mini`) |
| `E2E_GEMINI_MODEL` | `agents/gemini.go:52` | default `gemini-2.5-flash` (CI: `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`) |
| `E2E_OPENCODE_MODEL` | `agents/opencode.go:25` | default `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` |

**`E2E_CLAUDE_MODEL` does not exist.** Claude's model is hard-coded to `haiku` in `e2e/agents/claude.go:86` (`cfg := &runConfig{Model: "haiku"}`); the only override is per-call `agents.Option`. Same pattern for Copilot (`claude-haiku-4.5`, `copilot-cli.go:60`) and Droid (`custom:claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`, `droid.go:79`).

`E2E_PARALLEL=1` is set by `.github/workflows/e2e-windows.yml:44` but is **read by nothing** in the codebase — dead env var.

Also forced by `TestMain` (`e2e/tests/main_test.go`): `ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE=file`, `ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE_PATH`, `ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` (empty temp file), and `PATH` prefixed with the binary's dir so bare `entire` in git/agent hooks resolves to the test binary.

Locally: OAuth/keychain. | none | 1.0 |

Registers only if binary on PATH (`opencode.go:22`). `Bootstrap()` runs 3 warmup prompts (upstream DB-migration race #6935). | none | 2.0 |
| `gemini-cli` | `gemini` | `gemini` | `npm install -g @google/gemini-cli` | `GEMINI_API_KEY`. `Bootstrap()` is a no-op. Uses `GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE=true`. | 2 | 2.5 |

## 5. Binary: built from source, but overridable

- `e2e/entire/entire.go:16` — `BinPath()` reads **`E2E_ENTIRE_BIN`** and `log.Fatal`s if unset ("run tests via `mise run test:e2e`"). There is no PATH lookup fallback and no use of a system-installed `entire`.
- `mise-tasks/test/e2e/_default` sets it: **only if `E2E_ENTIRE_BIN` is already set does it skip `mise run build`.** So `E2E_ENTIRE_BIN=/path/to/entire mise run test:e2e ...` points the suite at a pre-installed binary and skips the build entirely. (The `canary` and `roger-roger` tasks always build and overwrite it.)
- `main_test.go` then (a) `ensureHookEntireBinary()` — creates a symlink (Unix) or file copy (Windows) named `entire`/`entire.exe` next to the resolved binary if the name differs, so hooks invoking bare `entire` hit the same build; (b) prepends that directory to `PATH`.
- Preflight in `TestMain` `os.Exit(1)`s if `git` (and `tmux` on non-Windows) or any registered agent's `Binary()` is missing from PATH.

## 6. Windows support

Yes — Windows is a first-class CI leg, not skipped.

- `.github/workflows/e2e-windows.yml` runs the **full suite** on `windows-latest` with `--agent claude-code`, and is invoked from `e2e.yml` via `uses: ./.github/workflows/e2e-windows.yml`. A Windows failure is classified RED (real regression) in the Slack notifier.
- `runtime.GOOS` usages in `e2e/`:

- There are **no `t.Skip` calls keyed on `runtime.GOOS`** in `e2e/tests/`. Instead, interactive tests skip via the nil session: `if session == nil { t.Skipf("agent %s does not support interactive mode", ...) }`. name: E2E Tests (Windows)

on:
  workflow_call:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      test:
        description: "Test name filter (regex)"
        required: false
        default: ""

concurrency:
  group: e2e-windows-tests
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  e2e-windows:
    runs-on: windows-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup mise
        uses: jdx/mise-action@f10502fc09dadecfefb962fff68ce77213930204 # v4

      - name: Install Claude Code
        run: |
          irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex
          "$env:USERPROFILE\.local\bin" | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_PATH -Encoding utf8 -Append

      - name: Bootstrap agent
        shell: bash
        env:
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
        run: go run ./e2e/bootstrap claude-code

      - name: Run isolated test
        shell: bash
        env:
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}/e2e-artifacts
          E2E_PARALLEL: 1
        run: |
          mkdir -p "$E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR"
          mise run test:e2e --agent claude-code "${{ inputs.test }}"

      - name: Upload artifacts
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7
        with:
          name: e2e-isolated-claude-code-${{ inputs.test }}
          path: e2e-artifacts/
          retention-days: 7
=====E2E=====
          fi

  e2e-tests:
    needs: matrix-setup
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 40
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
      # Needed by the copilot-cli leg. GitHub does not allow matrix expressions in
      # `permissions:`, so this scope is granted to every leg's GITHUB_TOKEN. The
      # token is kept away from non-copilot agents in two ways: it is only placed
      # in COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN for the copilot-cli leg (see env blocks below), and
      # checkout runs with persist-credentials: false so it is not left in
      # .git/config for an agent process to read.
      copilot-requests: write
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        agent: ${{ fromJson(needs.matrix-setup.outputs.agents) }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # Don't persist the (copilot-scoped) GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config, where
          # an agent process running in the checkout could read it.
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Setup mise
        uses: jdx/mise-action@f10502fc09dadecfefb962fff68ce77213930204 # v4

      - name: Install system dependencies
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y tmux

      - name: Install agent CLI
        run: |
          case "${{ matrix.agent }}" in
            claude-code) curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash ;;
            opencode)    curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash ;;
            gemini-cli)  npm install -g @google/gemini-cli ;;
            codex)       npm install -g @openai/codex ;;
            cursor-cli)  curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS | bash ;;
            factoryai-droid) curl -fsSL https://app.factory.ai/cli | sh ;;
            copilot-cli)  npm install -g @github/copilot  ;;
            roger-roger) ;; # installed by mise (see mise.toml)
          esac
          echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH

      - name: Verify roger-roger agent
        if: matrix.agent == 'roger-roger'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          echo "Verifying roger-roger binaries on PATH..."
          command -v roger-roger
          command -v entire-agent-roger-roger

      - name: Bootstrap agent
        if: matrix.agent != 'roger-roger'
        env:
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          GEMINI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GEMINI_API_KEY }}
          OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
          CURSOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CURSOR_API_KEY }}
          FACTORY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_API_KEY }}
          # Only the copilot-cli leg gets the token; other agents must not receive it.
          COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ matrix.agent == 'copilot-cli' && github.token || '' }}
        run: go run ./e2e/bootstrap

      - name: Run E2E Tests
        env:
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          GEMINI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GEMINI_API_KEY }}
          OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
          E2E_CODEX_MODEL: ${{ matrix.agent == 'codex' && 'gpt-5.4-mini' || '' }}
          E2E_GEMINI_MODEL: ${{ matrix.agent == 'gemini-cli' && 'gemini-3.1-flash-lite' || '' }}
          CURSOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CURSOR_API_KEY }}
          FACTORY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_API_KEY }}
          # Only the copilot-cli leg gets the token; other agents must not receive it.
          COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ matrix.agent == 'copilot-cli' && github.token || '' }}
          E2E_CONCURRENT_TEST_LIMIT: ${{ matrix.agent == 'gemini-cli' && '6' || matrix.agent == 'factoryai-droid' && '1' || matrix.agent == 'cursor-cli' && '2' || '' }}

        # which does NOT enable --rerun-fails. Routing it through the default
        # task (`test:e2e`) would retry a real regression and mask it.
        run: |
          if [ "${{ matrix.agent }}" = "roger-roger" ]; then
            mise run test:e2e:roger-roger TestExternalAgent

            mise run test:e2e --agent ${{ matrix.agent }}

        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7
        with:
          name: e2e-artifacts-${{ matrix.agent }}
          path: e2e/artifacts/
          retention-days: 7

#!/bin/sh
#MISE description="Run E2E tests: mise run test:e2e --agent claude-code [filter]"
#MISE quiet=true
#USAGE flag "--agent <agent>" help="Agent (claude-code, gemini-cli, opencode, cursor-cli, copilot-cli)" default="" env="E2E_AGENT"
#USAGE arg "[filter]" help="Test name filter (regex)" default=""

set -eu

export E2E_AGENT="${usage_agent:-}"

# Build from source with version info unless a pre-built binary is provided.
if [ -z "${E2E_ENTIRE_BIN:-}" ]; then
  mise run build
  if [ -f "$PWD/entire.exe" ]; then
    export E2E_ENTIRE_BIN="$PWD/entire.exe"
  else
    export E2E_ENTIRE_BIN="$PWD/entire"
  fi
fi

if [ -z "${E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR:-}" ]; then
  E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR="$PWD/e2e/artifacts/$(date +%Y-%m-%dT%H-%M-%S)"
fi
export E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR
mkdir -p "$E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR"
echo "artifacts: $E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR"

filter="${usage_filter:-}"

# Use an explicit package path without the "..." wildcard. The wildcard
# triggers a Go toolchain panic on Windows ARM64 in modload/search.go
# (slice bounds out of range) and a GetFileInformationByHandleEx error
# with relative paths.
#
# --rerun-fails retries only the tests that failed (one extra attempt) to
# absorb transient real-agent non-determinism. It requires --packages (so the
# package list can no longer be a trailing positional arg) and -count=1. The

	"context"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/entireio/cli/e2e/agents"
	"github.com/entireio/cli/e2e/testutil"
)

// TestMultiSessionManualCommit: two prompts create files, user commits manually.
func TestMultiSessionManualCommit(t *testing.T) {
	testutil.ForEachAgent(t, 3*time.Minute, func(t *testing.T, s *testutil.RepoState, ctx context.Context) {
		_, err := s.RunPrompt(t, ctx, "create a markdown file at docs/red.md with a paragraph about the colour red. Do not ask for confirmation, just make the change.")
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("agent prompt 1 failed: %v", err)
		}

		_, err = s.RunPrompt(t, ctx, "create a markdown file at docs/blue.md with a paragraph about the colour blue. Do not ask for confirmation, just make the change.")
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("agent prompt 2 failed: %v", err)
		}

		s.Git(t, "add", ".")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "Add md files about red and blue")

		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "docs/*.md")
		testutil.AssertNewCommits(t, s, 1)

		testutil.WaitForCheckpoint(t, s, 30*time.Second)
		testutil.AssertCheckpointAdvanced(t, s)

		cpID := testutil.AssertHasCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD")
		testutil.AssertCheckpointExists(t, s.Dir, cpID)
		testutil.WaitForNoShadowBranches(t, s.Dir, 10*time.Second)
	})
}

// TestMultiSessionSequential: two prompts each commit separately, distinct checkpoints.
func TestMultiSessionSequential(t *testing.T) {
	testutil.ForEachAgent(t, 3*time.Minute, func(t *testing.T, s *testutil.RepoState, ctx context.Context) {
		promptTimeout := 3 * time.Minute
		_, err := s.RunPrompt(t, ctx,
			"create a markdown file at docs/red.md about the colour red, then git add and git commit it with a short message. Do not ask for confirmation, just make the change. Do not include any trailers or metadata in the commit message. Do not use worktrees.",
			agents.WithPromptTimeout(promptTimeout))
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("agent prompt 1 failed: %v", err)
		}

		_, err = s.RunPrompt(t, ctx,
			"create a markdown file at docs/blue.md about the colour blue, then git add and git commit it with a short message. Do not ask for confirmation, just make the change. Do not include any trailers or metadata in the commit message. Do not use worktrees.",
			agents.WithPromptTimeout(promptTimeout))
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("agent prompt 2 failed: %v", err)
		}

		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "docs/*.md")

# Nightly install-and-smoke workflow (3 OSes × all agents)

## Context

Every existing E2E workflow (`e2e.yml`, `e2e-windows.yml`, `e2e-isolated.yml`, …) tests a
binary **built from source in the same checkout**. Nothing tests the artifact users actually
install. `nightly.yml` cuts a nightly tag at 06:00 UTC and `release.yml` publishes it to the
Homebrew tap, the `install.sh` nightly channel, and Scoop — and no job ever installs any of
those and checks the CLI still works.

This adds one nightly workflow that installs the published nightly CLI the way a user would
(brew / curl / PowerShell), points the existing E2E harness at that installed binary, and runs
a single smoke test per agent. It answers one question: *does the shipped nightly build still
checkpoint real agent work on macOS, Linux and Windows?*

## Shape

One job per OS (`matrix.os`), and inside each job a **sequential loop over that OS's agents**.
No agent submatrix — 3 jobs total. Sequential keeps API rate limits sane, keeps per-agent
failure attribution clean, and each agent run is one test (~2–4 min).

## The one test: `TestMultiSessionSequential`

`e2e/tests/multi_session_test.go:43` — an exact match for the described validation:

1. Prompt 1: create `docs/red.md`, then `git add` + `git commit` it.
2. Prompt 2: same for `docs/blue.md`.
3. Asserts exactly 2 new commits; `WaitForCheckpoint` + `AssertCheckpointAdvanced`.
4. Asserts a checkpoint trailer on `HEAD` **and** `HEAD~1`, both checkpoints exist, each has a
   single session, and the two sessions are distinct.
5. `WaitForNoShadowBranches` — no `entire/*` leftovers.

Runner-up considered and rejected: `TestMultiSessionManualCommit` (same 2 prompts but only one
user commit → one checkpoint, weaker signal) and `TestSingleSessionManualCommit` (one prompt).

Passed as the positional filter, which becomes `-run`:
`mise run test:e2e --agent <agent> TestMultiSessionSequential`.

## Key mechanism: `E2E_ENTIRE_BIN`

`mise-tasks/test/e2e/_default` runs `mise run build` **only when `E2E_ENTIRE_BIN` is unset**.
Exporting `E2E_ENTIRE_BIN=<path to installed entire>` into `$GITHUB_ENV` after the install step
therefore skips the build entirely and makes the whole suite — including the `entire` that git
hooks and agent hooks invoke (`ensureHookEntireBinary` + PATH prepend in
`e2e/tests/main_test.go`) — exercise the installed nightly. This is the entire point of the
workflow; without it the job silently tests a source build again.

## New file: `.github/workflows/nightly-e2e.yml`

- **Triggers**: `schedule: cron "0 9 * * *"` (3h after `nightly.yml`'s 06:00 tag, so
  `release.yml` has published), plus `workflow_dispatch` with optional `test` (default
  `TestMultiSessionSequential`) and `agents` (override the per-OS list) inputs.
- **`concurrency`**: `group: nightly-e2e`, `cancel-in-progress: true` (matches `e2e.yml`).
- **Job `smoke`**: `strategy: {fail-fast: false, matrix: {os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest,
  windows-latest]}}`, `runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}`, `timeout-minutes: 45`.
- **Permissions**: `contents: read`, `actions: read`, `copilot-requests: write` (needed by the
  copilot-cli iteration; GitHub forbids matrix expressions in `permissions:`, same constraint
  `e2e.yml` documents).

### Steps

1. **Checkout** — `actions/checkout` (pin the same SHA as `e2e.yml`), `ref: main`,
   `persist-credentials: false` (an agent process runs in this checkout and must not find the
   copilot-scoped token in `.git/config`).
2. **Setup mise** — `jdx/mise-action@f10502fc…` (v4), no options, same as every other E2E
   workflow. Go comes from `mise.toml` (1.26.6); no `actions/setup-go`.
3. **Install the nightly CLI** — one step per OS, `if: matrix.os == …`:
   - macOS: `brew tap entireio/tap && brew install --cask entire@nightly`
   - Linux: `curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash -s -- --channel nightly`, then
     `echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH`
   - Windows (`shell: pwsh`), written as if the script were already published:
     `& ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://entire.io/install.ps1))) -Channel nightly`, then
     append `"$env:USERPROFILE\.local\bin"` to `$env:GITHUB_PATH`. (`irm | iex` cannot take
     arguments, hence the scriptblock form.) **Implementing/hosting `install.ps1` is explicitly
     out of scope** — the Windows leg is expected red until someone publishes it.
4. **Pin `E2E_ENTIRE_BIN`** — resolve the installed binary and write it to `$GITHUB_ENV`
   (`command -v entire` on Unix, `(Get-Command entire).Source` on Windows), then run
   `entire version` so the log proves a `-nightly.*` build is under test.
5. **System deps** — `tmux` on Linux (`apt-get`) and macOS (`brew`). `TestMain`'s preflight
   hard-requires tmux on every non-Windows OS, even though `TestMultiSessionSequential` itself
   is headless.
6. **Install agents** — one `case`/`switch` per OS producing the list plus its installers,
   mirroring `e2e.yml`'s block:
   - `ubuntu-latest`: claude-code (`claude.ai/install.sh`), opencode, codex (npm), copilot-cli
     (npm), cursor-cli, factoryai-droid
   - `macos-latest`: claude-code, opencode, codex, copilot-cli, cursor-cli, factoryai-droid
     (all ship a mac curl/npm installer)
   - `windows-latest`: claude-code (`claude.ai/install.ps1`), codex (npm), copilot-cli (npm).
     cursor-cli and factoryai-droid are excluded — cursor-cli drives every prompt through tmux
     (`e2e/agents/cursor_cli.go`) and neither has a Windows installer.
   - Excluded everywhere, with the reason in a comment: **gemini-cli** (≥0.57.0 forces
     `core.hooksPath=''`, so no checkpoint is ever recorded — already excluded from `e2e.yml`),
     **pi** (no CI installer), **vogon** (built in-tree, not a shipped agent), **roger-roger**
     (deterministic protocol fixture; its prompt handling is not known to satisfy this test's
     "create a file then git commit it" instruction — add later only after verifying locally).
7. **Bootstrap + run loop** (`shell: bash` on all three OSes — Windows runners have Git Bash and
   `e2e-windows.yml` already does exactly this). For each agent in the OS's list:
   ```
   go run ./e2e/bootstrap "$agent"
   E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR="$PWD/e2e/artifacts/$agent" \
     mise run test:e2e --agent "$agent" "$TEST"
   ```
   with `set +e` around the run, a pass/fail recorded per agent, and the loop continuing on
   failure. After the loop: write a per-agent table to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` and `exit 1` if
   any agent failed. Per-agent `E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR` is required — the task derives one shared
   timestamped dir otherwise and later agents overwrite earlier reports.
   Env pins carried over from `e2e.yml`: `E2E_CODEX_MODEL=gpt-5.4-mini`, and
   `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` exported **only inside the copilot-cli iteration** (job-level would
   hand the token to every other agent process, which `e2e.yml` deliberately avoids).
   Secrets: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `CURSOR_API_KEY`, `FACTORY_API_KEY`.
8. **Upload artifacts** — `if: always()`, `actions/upload-artifact` (same pinned SHA),
   `name: nightly-e2e-${{ matrix.os }}`, `path: e2e/artifacts/`, `retention-days: 7`.
9. **Slack notify** — a `needs: [smoke]`, `if: always() && needs.smoke.result == 'failure'` job
   reusing `e2e.yml`'s `slackapi/slack-github-action` step and `secrets.E2E_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL`.
   Simpler than `e2e.yml`'s RED/YELLOW classifier: any failure here means the shipped nightly is
   broken on some OS.

## Files

- **New**: `.github/workflows/nightly-e2e.yml` — the only file this plan adds.
- **Read for reference, unchanged**: `.github/workflows/e2e.yml` (agent install `case`, secret
  names, model pins, artifact + Slack steps), `.github/workflows/e2e-windows.yml` (`shell: bash`
  on Windows, `install.ps1` PATH handling), `mise-tasks/test/e2e/_default` (`E2E_ENTIRE_BIN`
  contract), `e2e/tests/main_test.go` (preflight requirements), `scripts/install.sh` (the
  `--channel nightly` flag this mirrors).

## Verification

1. `actionlint .github/workflows/nightly-e2e.yml` (and the CodeQL `actions` workflow will lint
   it on the PR, since it watches `.github/workflows/**`).
2. Reproduce a leg locally before merging — this is the step that proves the mechanism:
   ```
   curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash -s -- --channel nightly
   entire version                      # expect vX.Y.Z-nightly.<stamp>.<sha>
   E2E_ENTIRE_BIN="$(command -v entire)" \
     mise run test:e2e --agent claude-code TestMultiSessionSequential
   ```
   Confirm the log shows no `mise run build` and that `e2e/artifacts/*/entire-version.txt`
   names the nightly binary, not a source build.
3. `workflow_dispatch` the new workflow on the branch before merge, with `test` left at its
   default. Expect ubuntu + macOS green and Windows red at the install step until
   `install.ps1` is published.

## Known caveats to state in the PR

- **Windows is expected red** until `https://entire.io/install.ps1` exists. Out of scope here.
- **Version skew**: tests are checked out from `main` while the binary is last night's nightly
  tag. Nightlies are cut from `main`, so the gap is one day; a harness change that depends on
  unreleased CLI behaviour will fail this workflow legitimately.
- `mise run test:e2e` keeps `--rerun-fails=1`, which absorbs one flaky agent turn. Appropriate
  for an unattended nightly; do not remove it here.
- The checkpoint backend is pinned to `git-branch` by `TestMain`'s default — this workflow does
  not exercise the `git-refs` backend that first-run `enable` now selects.

# Nightly install-and-smoke workflow (3 OSes × all agents)

## Context

Every existing E2E workflow (`e2e.yml`, `e2e-windows.yml`, `e2e-isolated.yml`, …) tests a
binary **built from source in the same checkout**. Nothing tests the artifact users actually
install. `nightly.yml` cuts a nightly tag at 06:00 UTC and `release.yml` publishes it to the
Homebrew tap, the `install.sh` nightly channel, and Scoop — and no job ever installs any of
those and checks the CLI still works.

This adds one nightly workflow that installs the published nightly CLI the way a user would
(brew / curl / PowerShell), points the existing E2E harness at that installed binary, and runs
a single smoke test per agent. It answers one question: *does the shipped nightly build still
checkpoint real agent work on macOS, Linux and Windows?*

## Shape

One job per OS (`matrix.os`), and inside each job a **sequential loop over that OS's agents**.
No agent submatrix — 3 jobs total. Sequential keeps API rate limits sane, keeps per-agent
failure attribution clean, and each agent run is one test (~2–4 min).

## The one test: `TestMultiSessionSequential`

`e2e/tests/multi_session_test.go:43` — an exact match for the described validation:

1. Prompt 1: create `docs/red.md`, then `git add` + `git commit` it.
2. Prompt 2: same for `docs/blue.md`.
3. Asserts exactly 2 new commits; `WaitForCheckpoint` + `AssertCheckpointAdvanced`.
4. Asserts a checkpoint trailer on `HEAD` **and** `HEAD~1`, both checkpoints exist, each has a
   single session, and the two sessions are distinct.
5. `WaitForNoShadowBranches` — no `entire/*` leftovers.

Runner-up considered and rejected: `TestMultiSessionManualCommit` (same 2 prompts but only one
user commit → one checkpoint, weaker signal) and `TestSingleSessionManualCommit` (one prompt).

Passed as the positional filter, which becomes `-run`:
`mise run test:e2e --agent <agent> TestMultiSessionSequential`.

## The checkout is pinned to the installed nightly's tag

The tests must match the binary, so the job **installs first and checks out second**, deriving
the ref from the binary itself rather than guessing "the latest nightly tag":

1. Install the nightly CLI (brew / curl / ps1 — all remote, no checkout needed yet).
2. `entire version` prints `Entire CLI <version>` on line 1. GoReleaser stamps
   `versioninfo.Version` with `{{.Version}}`, i.e. the tag **without** its leading `v`
   (`.goreleaser.yaml:25`), so the tag is `v` + that field:
   `TAG="v$(entire version | head -1 | awk '{print $3}')"`.
3. Fail the job if `$TAG` does not match `v*-nightly.*` — a stable or unparseable version means
   the install step resolved the wrong channel, and silently testing `main` instead would hide
   exactly the skew this pinning exists to remove. Fail closed, never fall back.
4. `actions/checkout` with `ref: ${{ env.NIGHTLY_TAG }}`.

`scripts/install.sh` has no `--version` flag (only `--channel`), so pinning the *install* to a
chosen tag is not possible — deriving the tag from the install is the direction that works.

## Key mechanism: `E2E_ENTIRE_BIN`

`mise-tasks/test/e2e/_default` runs `mise run build` **only when `E2E_ENTIRE_BIN` is unset**.
Exporting `E2E_ENTIRE_BIN=<path to installed entire>` into `$GITHUB_ENV` after the install step

- **`concurrency`**: `group: nightly-e2e`, `cancel-in-progress: true` (matches `e2e.yml`).
- **Job `smoke`**: `strategy: {fail-fast: false, matrix: {os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest,
  windows-latest]}}`, `runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}`, `timeout-minutes: 45`.
- **Permissions**: `contents: read`, `actions: read`, `copilot-requests: write` (needed by the
  copilot-cli iteration; GitHub forbids matrix expressions in `permissions:`, same constraint

   - macOS: `brew tap entireio/tap && brew install --cask entire@nightly`

   - `windows-latest`: claude-code (`claude.ai/install.ps1`), codex (npm), copilot-cli (npm).

     **pi** (no CI installer), **vogon** (built in-tree, not a shipped agent), **roger-roger**
     (deterministic protocol fixture; its prompt handling is not known to satisfy this test's
     "create a file then git commit it" instruction — add later only after verifying locally).
7. **Bootstrap + run loop** (`shell: bash` on all three OSes — Windows runners have Git Bash and

   ```
   go run ./e2e/bootstrap "$agent"

   ```

   hand the token to every other agent process, which `e2e.yml` deliberately avoids).
   Secrets: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `CURSOR_API_KEY`, `FACTORY_API_KEY`.
8. **Upload artifacts** — `if: always()`, `actions/upload-artifact` (same pinned SHA),

   Simpler than `e2e.yml`'s RED/YELLOW classifier: any failure here means the shipped nightly is

1. Prompt 1: create `docs/red.md`, then `git add` + `git commit` it.
2. Prompt 2: same for `docs/blue.md`.
3. Asserts exactly 2 new commits; `WaitForCheckpoint` + `AssertCheckpointAdvanced`.
4. Asserts a checkpoint trailer on `HEAD` **and** `HEAD~1`, both checkpoints exist, each has a
   single session, and the two sessions are distinct.
5. `WaitForNoShadowBranches` — no `entire/*` leftovers.

Runner-up considered and rejected: `TestMultiSessionManualCommit` (same 2 prompts but only one
user commit → one checkpoint, weaker signal) and `TestSingleSessionManualCommit` (one prompt).

Passed as the positional filter, which becomes `-run`:
`mise run test:e2e --agent <agent> TestMultiSessionSequential`.

## The checkout is pinned to the installed nightly's tag

The tests must match the binary, so the job **installs first and checks out second**, deriving
the ref from the binary itself rather than guessing "the latest nightly tag":

1. Install the nightly CLI (brew / curl / ps1 — all remote, no checkout needed yet).
2. `entire version` prints `Entire CLI <version>` on line 1. GoReleaser stamps
   `versioninfo.Version` with `{{.Version}}`, i.e. the tag **without** its leading `v`
   (`.goreleaser.yaml:25`), so the tag is `v` + that field:
   `TAG="v$(entire version | head -1 | awk '{print $3}')"`.
3. Fail the job if `$TAG` does not match `v*-nightly.*` — a stable or unparseable version means
   the install step resolved the wrong channel, and silently testing `main` instead would hide
   exactly the skew this pinning exists to remove. Fail closed, never fall back.
4. `actions/checkout` with `ref: ${{ env.NIGHTLY_TAG }}`.

Result: the harness, the mise toolchain pins, and the CLI under test all come from one commit.
`scripts/install.sh` has no `--version` flag (only `--channel`), so pinning the *install* to a
chosen tag is not possible — deriving the tag from the install is the direction that works.

## Key mechanism: `E2E_ENTIRE_BIN`

`mise-tasks/test/e2e/_default` runs `mise run build` **only when `E2E_ENTIRE_BIN` is unset**.
Exporting `E2E_ENTIRE_BIN=<path to installed entire>` into `$GITHUB_ENV` after the install step
therefore skips the build entirely and makes the whole suite — including the `entire` that git
hooks and agent hooks invoke (`ensureHookEntireBinary` + PATH prepend in
`e2e/tests/main_test.go`) — exercise the installed nightly. This is the entire point of the
workflow; without it the job silently tests a source build again.

## New file: `.github/workflows/nightly-e2e.yml`

- **Triggers**: `schedule: cron "0 9 * * *"` (3h after `nightly.yml`'s 06:00 tag, so
  `release.yml` has published), plus `workflow_dispatch` with optional `test` (default
  `TestMultiSessionSequential`) and `agents` (override the per-OS list) inputs.
- **`concurrency`**: `group: nightly-e2e`, `cancel-in-progress: true` (matches `e2e.yml`).
- **Job `smoke`**: `strategy: {fail-fast: false, matrix: {os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest,
  windows-latest]}}`, `runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}`, `timeout-minutes: 45`.
- **Permissions**: `contents: read`, `actions: read`, `copilot-requests: write` (needed by the
  copilot-cli iteration; GitHub forbids matrix expressions in `permissions:`, same constraint
  `e2e.yml` documents).

### Steps

1. **Install the nightly CLI** — one step per OS, `if: matrix.os == …`, before any checkout:
   - macOS: `brew tap entireio/tap && brew install --cask entire@nightly`
   - Linux: `curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash -s -- --channel nightly`, then
     `echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH`
   - Windows (`shell: pwsh`), written as if the script were already published:
     `& ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://entire.io/install.ps1))) -Channel nightly`, then
     append `"$env:USERPROFILE\.local\bin"` to `$env:GITHUB_PATH`. (`irm | iex` cannot take
     arguments, hence the scriptblock form.) **Implementing/hosting `install.ps1` is explicitly
     out of scope** — the Windows leg is expected red until someone publishes it.
2. **Resolve tag + binary path** — run `entire version`, derive `NIGHTLY_TAG` as described
   above (failing closed if it is not a `v*-nightly.*` version), and resolve the binary path
   (`command -v entire` / `(Get-Command entire).Source`). Write both to `$GITHUB_ENV` as
   `NIGHTLY_TAG` and `E2E_ENTIRE_BIN`, and echo the full version into the log.
3. **Checkout** — `actions/checkout` (same pinned SHA as `e2e.yml`),
   `ref: ${{ env.NIGHTLY_TAG }}`, `persist-credentials: false` (an agent process runs in this
   checkout and must not find the copilot-scoped token in `.git/config`).
4. **Setup mise** — `jdx/mise-action@f10502fc…` (v4), no options, same as every other E2E
   workflow. Go comes from the checked-out tag's `mise.toml`; no `actions/setup-go`.
5. **System deps** — `tmux` on Linux (`apt-get`) and macOS (`brew`). `TestMain`'s preflight
   hard-requires tmux on every non-Windows OS, even though `TestMultiSessionSequential` itself
   is headless.
6. **Install agents** — one `case`/`switch` per OS producing the list plus its installers,
   mirroring `e2e.yml`'s block:
   - `ubuntu-latest`: claude-code (`claude.ai/install.sh`), opencode, codex (npm), copilot-cli
     (npm), cursor-cli, factoryai-droid
   - `macos-latest`: claude-code, opencode, codex, copilot-cli, cursor-cli, factoryai-droid
     (all ship a mac curl/npm installer)
   - `windows-latest`: claude-code (`claude.ai/install.ps1`), codex (npm), copilot-cli (npm).
     cursor-cli and factoryai-droid are excluded — cursor-cli drives every prompt through tmux
     (`e2e/agents/cursor_cli.go`) and neither has a Windows installer.
   - Excluded everywhere, with the reason in a comment: **gemini-cli** (≥0.57.0 forces
     `core.hooksPath=''`, so no checkpoint is ever recorded — already excluded from `e2e.yml`),
     **pi** (no CI installer), **vogon** (built in-tree, not a shipped agent), **roger-roger**
     (deterministic protocol fixture; its prompt handling is not known to satisfy this test's
     "create a file then git commit it" instruction — add later only after verifying locally).
7. **Bootstrap + run loop** (`shell: bash` on all three OSes — Windows runners have Git Bash and
   `e2e-windows.yml` already does exactly this). For each agent in the OS's list:
   ```
   go run ./e2e/bootstrap "$agent"
   E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR="$PWD/e2e/artifacts/$agent" \
     mise run test:e2e --agent "$agent" "$TEST"
   ```
   with `set +e` around the run, a pass/fail recorded per agent, and the loop continuing on
   failure. After the loop: write a per-agent table to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` and `exit 1` if
   any agent failed. Per-agent `E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR` is required — the task derives one shared
   timestamped dir otherwise and later agents overwrite earlier reports.
   Env pins carried over from `e2e.yml`: `E2E_CODEX_MODEL=gpt-5.4-mini`, and
   `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` exported **only inside the copilot-cli iteration** (job-level would
   hand the token to every other agent process, which `e2e.yml` deliberately avoids).
   Secrets: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `CURSOR_API_KEY`, `FACTORY_API_KEY`.
8. **Upload artifacts** — `if: always()`, `actions/upload-artifact` (same pinned SHA),
   `name: nightly-e2e-${{ matrix.os }}`, `path: e2e/artifacts/`, `retention-days: 7`.
9. **Slack notify** — a `needs: [smoke]`, `if: always() && needs.smoke.result == 'failure'` job
   reusing `e2e.yml`'s `slackapi/slack-github-action` step and `secrets.E2E_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL`.
   Simpler than `e2e.yml`'s RED/YELLOW classifier: any failure here means the shipped nightly is
   broken on some OS.

## Files

- **New**: `.github/workflows/nightly-e2e.yml` — the only file this plan adds.
- **Read for reference, unchanged**: `.github/workflows/e2e.yml` (agent install `case`, secret
  names, model pins, artifact + Slack steps), `.github/workflows/e2e-windows.yml` (`shell: bash`
  on Windows, `install.ps1` PATH handling), `mise-tasks/test/e2e/_default` (`E2E_ENTIRE_BIN`
  contract), `e2e/tests/main_test.go` (preflight requirements), `scripts/install.sh` (the
  `--channel nightly` flag this mirrors).

## Verification

1. `actionlint .github/workflows/nightly-e2e.yml` (and the CodeQL `actions` workflow will lint
   it on the PR, since it watches `.github/workflows/**`).
2. Reproduce a leg locally before merging — this is the step that proves the mechanism:
   ```
   curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash -s -- --channel nightly
   entire version                      # expect vX.Y.Z-nightly.<stamp>.<sha>
   TAG="v$(entire version | head -1 | awk '{print $3}')"
   git checkout "$TAG"                 # same pin the workflow applies
   E2E_ENTIRE_BIN="$(command -v entire)" \
     mise run test:e2e --agent claude-code TestMultiSessionSequential
   ```
   Confirm the log shows no `mise run build` and that `e2e/artifacts/*/entire-version.txt`
   names the nightly binary, not a source build.
3. `workflow_dispatch` the new workflow on the branch before merge, with `test` left at its
   default. Expect ubuntu + macOS green and Windows red at the install step until
   `install.ps1` is published.

## Known caveats to state in the PR

- **Windows is expected red** until `https://entire.io/install.ps1` exists. Out of scope here.
- **No version skew by construction**: the checkout ref is derived from the installed binary's
  own version stamp, so a failure is always the release's fault, never a harness/binary
  mismatch. The flip side: a harness bug fixed on `main` today keeps failing this workflow
  until the next nightly ships.
- `mise run test:e2e` keeps `--rerun-fails=1`, which absorbs one flaky agent turn. Appropriate
  for an unattended nightly; do not remove it here.
- The checkpoint backend is pinned to `git-branch` by `TestMain`'s default — this workflow does
  not exercise the `git-refs` backend that first-run `enable` now selects.

name: E2E Tests

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agent:
        description: 'Run a single agent (leave empty for all)'
        required: false
        type: choice
        options:
          - ''
          - claude-code
          - opencode
          - gemini-cli
          - factoryai-droid
          - cursor-cli
          - copilot-cli
          - roger-roger
          - codex
  push:
    branches:
      - main

# Concurrency: only one E2E job runs at a time
concurrency:
  group: e2e-tests
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  # Build the matrix dynamically so workflow_dispatch can select a single agent.
  matrix-setup:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      agents: ${{ steps.set.outputs.agents }}
    steps:
      - id: set
        # Pass the input through env rather than interpolating it into the script:
        # `type: choice` only constrains the UI, so a REST-API dispatch could inject
        # shell metacharacters here otherwise.
        env:
          AGENT_INPUT: ${{ github.event.inputs.agent }}
        # gemini-cli is deliberately absent from the all-agents list. Since
        # Gemini CLI 0.57.0 the agent forces `core.hooksPath=''` on every shell
        # command it runs, so no checkpoint is recorded for a commit it makes and
        # the leg fails for a reason no change on our side can fix. It stays in
        # the workflow_dispatch choices above so the leg can be run by hand
        # against a newer Gemini release; put it back in this list (it is still
        # in the RED "reliable" tier in notify-slack) once one restores hooks.
        run: |
          input="$AGENT_INPUT"
          if [ -n "$input" ]; then
            echo "agents=[\"$input\"]" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo 'agents=["claude-code","opencode","factoryai-droid","cursor-cli","copilot-cli","roger-roger","codex"]' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
====SLACK====
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Reliable tier (RED). The e2e-windows reusable job is also RED but
          # is matched separately below since it has no "(agent)" suffix.
          reliable="claude-code opencode gemini-cli roger-roger"

          failed_names=$(gh api --paginate \
            "repos/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}/jobs" \
            --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .name')

          red=""
          yellow=""
          while IFS= read -r name; do
            [ -z "$name" ] && continue
            case "$name" in
              *e2e-windows*) red="$red windows"; continue ;;
            esac
            # "e2e-tests (cursor-cli)" -> "cursor-cli"
            agent="${name#*(}"; agent="${agent%)*}"
            case " $reliable " in
              *" $agent "*) red="$red $agent" ;;
              *)            yellow="$yellow $agent" ;;
            esac
          done <<EOF
          $failed_names
          EOF

          # Each list was built as " a b c" (leading space, space-separated).
          # Strip the leading space, then join on ", ". Empty stays empty.
          red="${red# }";       red="${red// /, }"
          yellow="${yellow# }"; yellow="${yellow// /, }"

          if [ -n "$red" ]; then
            color="#d50200"
            header=":red_circle: *E2E Tests Failed* on \`main\`"
          else
            color="#daa038"
            header=":large_yellow_circle: *E2E flaky-agent failures* on \`main\`"
          fi

          body=""
          [ -n "$red" ]    && body="${body}Reliable agents (regression): *${red}*\\n"
          [ -n "$yellow" ] && body="${body}Flaky agents (investigate): *${yellow}*\\n"

          {
            echo "color=$color"
            echo "header=$header"
            echo "body=$body"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Notify Slack of E2E failure
        uses: slackapi/slack-github-action@dcb1066f776dd043e64d0e8ba94ca15cc7e1875d # v4.0.0
        with:
          webhook: ${{ secrets.E2E_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL }}
          webhook-type: incoming-webhook

                {
                  "color": "${{ steps.classify.outputs.color }}",
                  "blocks": [
                    {
                      "type": "section",
                      "text": {
                        "type": "mrkdwn",
                        "text": "${{ steps.classify.outputs.header }}\n\n${{ steps.classify.outputs.body }}<${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}|View run details>"
                      }

                        }
                      ]
                    }
                  ]
                }
              ]
            }

cat > .github/workflows/nightly-e2e.yml <<'YAML'
name: Nightly Install Smoke

# Every other E2E workflow tests a binary built from source in the same
# checkout. This one installs the *published* nightly the way a user would
# (brew / curl / PowerShell), points the existing E2E harness at that installed
# binary via E2E_ENTIRE_BIN, and runs a single smoke test per agent on each OS.
#
# It answers one question: does the shipped nightly build still checkpoint real
# agent work on Linux, macOS and Windows?

on:
  schedule:
    # 3h after nightly.yml cuts the tag at 06:00 UTC, so release.yml has
    # published the artifacts this workflow installs.
    - cron: "0 9 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      test:
        description: "Test name filter (regex)"
        required: false
        default: "TestMultiSessionSequential"

concurrency:
  group: nightly-install-smoke
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  smoke:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 60
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
      # Needed by the copilot-cli leg. GitHub does not allow matrix expressions
      # in `permissions:`, so the scope is granted to every OS leg's
      # GITHUB_TOKEN. The token is only ever placed in an environment a copilot
      # process can see by the dedicated copilot step below, and checkout runs
      # with persist-credentials: false so it is not left in .git/config.
      copilot-requests: write
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]

    steps:
      # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
      # 1. Install the published nightly CLI. No checkout yet: the ref we check
      #    out is derived from the version of the binary installed here.
      # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
      - name: Install nightly CLI (Linux)
        if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash -s -- --channel nightly
          echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Install nightly CLI (macOS)
        if: matrix.os == 'macos-latest'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          brew tap entireio/tap
          brew install --cask entire@nightly

      # There is no nightly channel for Windows today: the Scoop bucket ships
      # stable only and install.ps1 is not published yet. This step is written
      # as if it were; the Windows leg stays red until someone hosts it.
      - name: Install nightly CLI (Windows)
        if: matrix.os == 'windows-latest'
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          # irm | iex cannot take arguments, hence the scriptblock form.
          & ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://entire.io/install.ps1))) -Channel nightly
          "$env:USERPROFILE\.local\bin" | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_PATH -Encoding utf8 -Append

      # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
      # 2. Pin the checkout to the tag that produced the installed binary, so
      #    the harness and the CLI under test come from one commit.
      # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
      - name: Resolve nightly tag and binary path (Unix)
        if: matrix.os != 'windows-latest'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          entire version
          version=$(entire version | head -1 | awk '{print $3}')
          tag="v$version"
          # Fail closed. A stable or unparseable version means the install
          # resolved the wrong channel; silently testing main instead would
          # hide exactly the skew this pin exists to remove.
          case "$tag" in
            v*-nightly.*) ;;
            *) echo "expected a v*-nightly.* version, got '$tag'" >&2; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          {
            echo "NIGHTLY_TAG=$tag"
            echo "E2E_ENTIRE_BIN=$(command -v entire)"
          } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Resolve nightly tag and binary path (Windows)
        if: matrix.os == 'windows-latest'
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
          entire version
          $version = (entire version | Select-Object -First 1).Split(" ")[2]
          $tag = "v$version"
          if ($tag -notlike "v*-nightly.*") {
            Write-Error "expected a v*-nightly.* version, got '$tag'"
          }
          "NIGHTLY_TAG=$tag" | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_ENV -Encoding utf8 -Append
          "E2E_ENTIRE_BIN=$((Get-Command entire).Source)" | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_ENV -Encoding utf8 -Append

      - name: Checkout the nightly tag
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.NIGHTLY_TAG }}
          # Don't persist the (copilot-scoped) GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config,
          # where an agent process running in the checkout could read it.
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Setup mise
        uses: jdx/mise-action@f10502fc09dadecfefb962fff68ce77213930204 # v4

      # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
      # 3. Test dependencies. tmux is a hard preflight requirement of the e2e
      #    TestMain on every non-Windows OS, even for headless tests.
      # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
      - name: Install tmux (Linux)
        if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y tmux

      - name: Install tmux (macOS)
        if: matrix.os == 'macos-latest'
        run: brew install tmux

      # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
      # 4. Agents. The per-OS list is limited to agents that actually install
      #    on that OS.
      #
      #    Excluded everywhere:
      #      gemini-cli   — since 0.57.0 it forces core.hooksPath='' on shell
      #                     commands, so no checkpoint is ever recorded (same
      #                     exclusion e2e.yml documents).
      #      pi           — no CI installer.
      #      vogon        — built in-tree, not a shipped agent.
      #      roger-roger  — deterministic protocol fixture; only exercises the
      #                     external-agent tests, not this smoke test.
      # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
      - name: Install agent CLIs (Unix)
        if: matrix.os != 'windows-latest'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash
          curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash
          curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS | bash
          curl -fsSL https://app.factory.ai/cli | sh
          npm install -g @openai/codex @github/copilot
          echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          echo "AGENTS=claude-code opencode codex cursor-cli factoryai-droid copilot-cli" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      # cursor-cli drives every prompt through tmux and factoryai-droid has no
      # Windows installer, so neither is in the Windows list.
      - name: Install agent CLIs (Windows)
        if: matrix.os == 'windows-latest'
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
          irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex
          "$env:USERPROFILE\.local\bin" | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_PATH -Encoding utf8 -Append
          npm install -g @openai/codex @github/copilot
          "AGENTS=claude-code codex copilot-cli" | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_ENV -Encoding utf8 -Append

      # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
      # 5. Run the smoke test once per agent, sequentially. Each agent gets its
      #    own artifact dir — the mise task derives a single timestamped one
      #    otherwise and later agents would overwrite earlier reports.
      #
      #    E2E_ENTIRE_BIN (set above) is what makes this test the *installed*
      #    nightly: mise-tasks/test/e2e/_default skips `mise run build` when it
      #    is already set, and TestMain puts that binary's directory on PATH so
      #    the git and agent hooks resolve to it too.
      #
      #    copilot-cli runs in its own step below so that the GitHub token it
      #    needs never appears in the environment of the other agents.
      # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
      - name: Run smoke test per agent
        shell: bash
        env:
          TEST_FILTER: ${{ github.event.inputs.test || 'TestMultiSessionSequential' }}
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
          CURSOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CURSOR_API_KEY }}
          FACTORY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_API_KEY }}
          E2E_CODEX_MODEL: gpt-5.4-mini
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail
          : > "$RUNNER_TEMP/results.txt"
          for agent in $AGENTS; do
            [ "$agent" = "copilot-cli" ] && continue
            echo "::group::$agent"
            go run ./e2e/bootstrap "$agent"
            E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR="$PWD/e2e/artifacts/$agent" \
              mise run test:e2e --agent "$agent" "$TEST_FILTER"
            rc=$?
            echo "$agent $rc" >> "$RUNNER_TEMP/results.txt"
            echo "::endgroup::"
          done

      - name: Run smoke test for copilot-cli
        if: contains(env.AGENTS, 'copilot-cli')
        shell: bash
        env:
          TEST_FILTER: ${{ github.event.inputs.test || 'TestMultiSessionSequential' }}
          COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail
          go run ./e2e/bootstrap copilot-cli
          E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR="$PWD/e2e/artifacts/copilot-cli" \
            mise run test:e2e --agent copilot-cli "$TEST_FILTER"
          echo "copilot-cli $?" >> "$RUNNER_TEMP/results.txt"

      - name: Summarize
        if: always()
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail
          failed=0
          {
            echo "### ${{ matrix.os }} — \`${NIGHTLY_TAG:-unknown}\`"
            echo ""
            echo "| agent | result |"
            echo "| --- | --- |"
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          while read -r agent rc; do
            [ -z "$agent" ] && continue
            if [ "$rc" = "0" ]; then
              echo "| $agent | ✅ pass |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            else
              echo "| $agent | ❌ fail (exit $rc) |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
              failed=1
            fi
          done < "$RUNNER_TEMP/results.txt"
          exit "$failed"

      - name: Upload artifacts
        if: always()

        with:

input.command:
gh pr create --draft --base main --head add-nightly-matrix-e2e-test --title "Nightly smoke test of the installed CLI across Linux, macOS and Windows" --body-file - <<'MD'
## Why

Every existing E2E workflow (`e2e.yml`, `e2e-windows.yml`, `e2e-isolated.yml`, …) tests a binary **built from source in the same checkout**. Nothing tests the artifact users actually install. `nightly.yml` cuts a tag at 06:00 UTC and `release.yml` publishes it to the Homebrew tap, the `install.sh` nightly channel and Scoop — and no job ever installs any of those and checks the CLI still works.

This adds one scheduled workflow that answers a single question: *does the shipped nightly build still checkpoint real agent work on Linux, macOS and Windows?*

## What it does

`.github/workflows/nightly-e2e.yml` (the only file added):

- **Trigger** — `schedule: 0 9 * * *`, three hours after `nightly.yml` tags, so `release.yml` has published. Also `workflow_dispatch` with a `test` filter input.
- **One job per OS** (`ubuntu-latest`, `macos-latest`, `windows-latest`), `fail-fast: false`, with a sequential per-agent loop inside each — no agent submatrix, 3 jobs total.
- **Installs the nightly the way a user would**: `brew install --cask entire@nightly`, `install.sh --channel nightly`, and on Windows `install.ps1 -Channel nightly`.
- **Pins the checkout to the installed binary's tag.** `entire version` is parsed into `NIGHTLY_TAG` and that is the checkout ref, so the harness and the CLI under test always come from one commit. It fails closed unless the version matches `v*-nightly.*` — a stable or unparseable version means the install resolved the wrong channel, and silently testing `main` instead would hide exactly the skew the pin exists to remove.
- **Points the harness at the installed binary** via `E2E_ENTIRE_BIN`. `mise-tasks/test/e2e/_default` skips `mise run build` when it is already set, and `TestMain` puts that binary's directory on `PATH` so git and agent hooks resolve to it too. Without this the job would silently test a source build again.

## The one test: `TestMultiSessionSequential`

`e2e/tests/multi_session_test.go:43` — two prompts, each creating a file and committing it, then asserting exactly two new commits, a checkpoint trailer on both `HEAD` and `HEAD~1`, both checkpoints existing with a single session each, the two sessions distinct, and no leftover `entire/*` shadow branches.

Considered and rejected: `TestMultiSessionManualCommit` (two prompts but one commit → one checkpoint, weaker signal) and `TestSingleSessionManualCommit` (one prompt).

## Agents

| OS | agents |
| --- | --- |
| ubuntu-latest | claude-code, opencode, codex, cursor-cli, factoryai-droid, copilot-cli |
| macos-latest | same six |
| windows-latest | claude-code, codex, copilot-cli |

cursor-cli drives every prompt through tmux and factoryai-droid has no Windows installer, so neither is in the Windows list. Excluded everywhere, with the reason in a comment: **gemini-cli** (since 0.57.0 it forces `core.hooksPath=''`, so no checkpoint is recorded — the same exclusion `e2e.yml` documents), **pi** (no CI installer), **vogon** (built in-tree), **roger-roger** (deterministic protocol fixture; only exercises the external-agent tests).

`copilot-cli` runs in its own step so `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` never enters the environment of the other agent processes — a single job-level env would have handed it to every agent, which `e2e.yml` deliberately avoids.

## Known caveats

- **Windows is expected red** until `https://entire.io/install.ps1` is published. There is no nightly Windows channel today — the Scoop bucket ships stable only (`skip_upload: auto`, no `entire@nightly` manifest). The step is written as if the script were already there; hosting it is out of scope for this PR.
- **No version skew by construction**, but the flip side: a harness fix landing on `main` today will not be picked up until the next nightly ships.
- `mise run test:e2e` keeps `--rerun-fails=1`, which absorbs one flaky agent turn. Appropriate for an unattended nightly.
- The checkpoint backend is pinned to `git-branch` by `TestMain`'s default, so this does not exercise the `git-refs` backend that first-run `enable` now selects.

## Verification

YAML parses and every bash block passes `bash -n`. No Go files changed, so `lint`/`test:ci` are not implicated; the CodeQL `actions` workflow lints `.github/workflows/**` on this PR.

Still to do before this leaves draft — please `workflow_dispatch` it on this branch:

```

entire version                                  # expect vX.Y.Z-nightly.<stamp>.<sha>
TAG="v$(entire version | head -1 | awk '{print $3}')"
git checkout "$TAG"
E2E_ENTIRE_BIN="$(command -v entire)" \
  mise run test:e2e --agent claude-code TestMultiSessionSequential
```

Confirm the log shows no `mise run build` and that `e2e/artifacts/*/entire-version.txt` names the nightly binary. Expect ubuntu + macOS green and Windows red at the install step.

### Windows

Install with Windows PowerShell 5.1 or later:

```powershell
irm https://entire.io/install.ps1 | iex  # stable
# or nightly:
# iex "& {$(irm https://entire.io/install.ps1)} -Channel nightly"
```

For stable releases, the PowerShell installer uses Scoop when it is available,
adding the Entire bucket if needed. Without Scoop — and for nightly releases —
it verifies the release checksum and installs both `entire.exe` and
`git-remote-entire.exe` to `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin`, adding that directory to
your user `PATH` if needed.

Or install the stable release with Scoop:

```powershell
scoop bucket add entire https://github.com/entireio/scoop-bucket.git
scoop install entire/entire
```

#### Migrating an old `cli` Scoop install (package rename)

The Scoop package was renamed from `cli` to `entire`. If your install is still registered as the old `cli` package, run the migration below. It installs the new package before removing the old one, so the old install is only removed once the new one is in place (`scoop reset` re-links the shared `entire.exe` and `git-remote-entire.exe` shims). Run it where `entire` is **not** running — a live `entire.exe` locks its own shim, so Scoop can't relink or uninstall it mid-run:

```powershell
cmd.exe /D /C "scoop install entire/entire && scoop uninstall entire/cli && scoop reset entire"
```

If the first step fails with "couldn't find manifest", your bucket clone predates the renamed package — run `scoop update` to refresh it, then retry the command above. Nothing is removed until the install succeeds, so a failed attempt leaves your existing install working.

### Go (development/manual setup)

```bash
go install github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire@latest

# The git remote helper that resolves entire:// URLs, needed for `entire repo clone`
# and `git clone entire://…`. The packaged installs above bundle it.
go install github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/git-remote-entire@latest

# Add Go binaries to PATH (add to ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc if not already configured)
export PATH="$HOME/go/bin:$PATH"
```

Install both, or just `entire` if you never clone over `entire://`. Git finds the helper by name on `$PATH`, which is what `go install` produces, so nothing else needs configuring.

One difference from a stable release: a `go install` build leaves [experimental commands](#experimental-commands) visible in `entire help`, the same as a nightly or a local build.

### Enable in your project

```bash
cd your-project && entire enable

# Check status
entire status
```

gh pr edit 2159 --body-file - <<'MD'
## Why

Every existing E2E workflow (`e2e.yml`, `e2e-windows.yml`, `e2e-isolated.yml`, …) tests a binary **built from source in the same checkout**. Nothing tests the artifact users actually install. `nightly.yml` cuts a tag at 06:00 UTC and `release.yml` publishes it to the Homebrew tap, the `install.sh` nightly channel, `install.ps1` and Scoop — and no job ever installs any of those and checks the CLI still works.

This adds one scheduled workflow that answers a single question: *does the shipped nightly build still checkpoint real agent work on Linux, macOS and Windows?*

## What it does

`.github/workflows/nightly-e2e.yml` (the only file added):

- **Trigger** — `schedule: 0 9 * * *`, three hours after `nightly.yml` tags, so `release.yml` has published. Also `workflow_dispatch` with a `test` filter input.
- **One job per OS** (`ubuntu-latest`, `macos-latest`, `windows-latest`), `fail-fast: false`, with a sequential per-agent loop inside each — no agent submatrix, 3 jobs total.
- **Installs the nightly exactly as the README documents it**: `brew install --cask entire@nightly`, `install.sh --channel nightly`, and `iex "& {$(irm https://entire.io/install.ps1)} -Channel nightly"`. On Windows a nightly always takes `install.ps1`'s verified-release-archive path into `$HOME\.local\bin`, since the Scoop bucket publishes stable only.
- **Pins the checkout to the installed binary's tag.** `entire version` is parsed into `NIGHTLY_TAG` and that is the checkout ref, so the harness and the CLI under test always come from one commit. It fails closed unless the version matches `v*-nightly.*` — a stable or unparseable version means the install resolved the wrong channel, and silently testing `main` instead would hide exactly the skew the pin exists to remove.
- **Points the harness at the installed binary** via `E2E_ENTIRE_BIN`. `mise-tasks/test/e2e/_default` skips `mise run build` when it is already set, and `TestMain` puts that binary's directory on `PATH` so git and agent hooks resolve to it too. Without this the job would silently test a source build again.

This is complementary to `install-ps1-e2e.yml`, which tests the installer script itself. This workflow tests what the installer *installed*.

## The one test: `TestMultiSessionSequential`

`e2e/tests/multi_session_test.go:43` — two prompts, each creating a file and committing it, then asserting exactly two new commits, a checkpoint trailer on both `HEAD` and `HEAD~1`, both checkpoints existing with a single session each, the two sessions distinct, and no leftover `entire/*` shadow branches.

Considered and rejected: `TestMultiSessionManualCommit` (two prompts but one commit → one checkpoint, weaker signal) and `TestSingleSessionManualCommit` (one prompt).

## Agents

| OS | agents |
| --- | --- |
| ubuntu-latest | claude-code, opencode, codex, cursor-cli, factoryai-droid, copilot-cli |
| macos-latest | same six |
| windows-latest | claude-code, codex, copilot-cli |

cursor-cli drives every prompt through tmux and factoryai-droid has no Windows installer, so neither is in the Windows list. Excluded everywhere, with the reason in a comment: **gemini-cli** (since 0.57.0 it forces `core.hooksPath=''`, so no checkpoint is recorded — the same exclusion `e2e.yml` documents), **pi** (no CI installer), **vogon** (built in-tree), **roger-roger** (deterministic protocol fixture; only exercises the external-agent tests).

`copilot-cli` runs in its own step so `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` never enters the environment of the other agent processes — a single job-level env would have handed it to every agent, which `e2e.yml` deliberately avoids.

## Known caveats

- **No version skew by construction**, but the flip side: a harness fix landing on `main` today will not be picked up until the next nightly ships.
- `mise run test:e2e` keeps `--rerun-fails=1`, which absorbs one flaky agent turn. Appropriate for an unattended nightly.
- The checkpoint backend is pinned to `git-branch` by `TestMain`'s default, so this does not exercise the `git-refs` backend that first-run `enable` now selects.

## Verification

YAML parses and every bash block passes `bash -n`. No Go files changed, so `lint`/`test:ci` are not implicated; the CodeQL `actions` workflow lints `.github/workflows/**` on this PR.

Still to do before this leaves draft — please `workflow_dispatch` it on this branch. The local equivalent of one leg:

entire version                                  # expect vX.Y.Z-nightly.<stamp>.<sha>
TAG="v$(entire version | head -1 | awk '{print $3}')"
git checkout "$TAG"
E2E_ENTIRE_BIN="$(command -v entire)" \
  mise run test:e2e --agent claude-code TestMultiSessionSequential
```

webhook that needs no token at all.

anyway.

Windows API. The bash-only paths in the same steps (`mkdir -p e2e/artifacts`, the
`e2e/artifacts/results.txt` reads and writes, and `upload-artifact`'s `path:`) stay relative —
they are handled by Git Bash and by the action, never by Go, so they were never affected.

**Six on Linux and macOS, three on Windows — 15 agent runs total across the three jobs.**

| OS | agents | count |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ubuntu-latest | claude-code, opencode, codex, cursor-cli, factoryai-droid, copilot-cli | 6 |
| macos-latest | same six | 6 |
| windows-latest | claude-code, codex, copilot-cli | 3 |

Each runs `TestMultiSessionSequential` once, sequentially within its job (copilot-cli in a separate step so its token stays out of the other agents' environment).

Windows drops cursor-cli (every prompt goes through tmux) and factoryai-droid (no Windows installer). Excluded everywhere: gemini-cli (forces `core.hooksPath=''` since 0.57.0, so nothing is checkpointed — same exclusion `e2e.yml` carries), pi (no CI installer), vogon (built in-tree), roger-roger (only exercises the external-agent tests).
I would just pick one, claude-code. Why are we running 6 or 3? is there anything I am missing from that decision?

You're not missing much — the six came from your original ask ("run it for all the built-in agents instead of just claude-code"), not from an independent argument that breadth pays here. Looking at it again, I think one agent is the better call, for a specific reason:

**What this workflow uniquely tests is the packaging, not the agents.** The install channel changes which bytes end up on disk. Agent-specific logic — hook wiring, transcript parsing, per-agent quirks — is identical whichever way the binary arrived, and `e2e.yml` already runs the full suite across all seven agents on every push to main. Running six agents here mostly re-buys coverage you already have, on a slower cadence.

**And breadth actively hurts a release signal.** 15 real-API agent runs a night, each with its own flake profile (cursor-cli is rate-limited, droid is serialized to one at a time), all feeding one Slack alert. When it goes red you can't tell "the nightly build is broken" from "droid was flaky again" without opening the run. claude-code is in `e2e.yml`'s own RED "reliable" tier — it's the agent whose failure means something.

**The one real thing you'd give up**: per-agent hook installation on macOS and Windows. `e2e.yml` is Linux-only and `e2e-windows.yml` is claude-code-only, so **macOS has no E2E coverage at all today** — the six-agent macOS leg would have been the first. That's a genuine gap, but it's a coverage gap that wants its own decision (extend `e2e.yml`'s matrix to macOS runners), not something to smuggle into a release smoke test where it makes failures ambiguous.

Trimming to claude-code also collapses two pieces of complexity: the per-agent loop becomes a single run, and the separate copilot-cli step exists only to keep `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` away from other agents — with no other agents, that step and the `copilot-requests: write` permission both go away.

Say go and I'll trim it: 3 jobs, one test each, and the workflow gets noticeably simpler.
